title: Putin Vows Retribution for Attacks on Russian Data Centers While Downplaying Damage to Refineries
key_facts: President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday 15 Oct 2026, by video link to the Delovaya Rossiya business association, that Russia is retaliating for Ukrainian attacks on its data centres: 'They took the first step and we began to answer' (Moscow Times).
These are his first public comments acknowledging drone attacks on Yandex and Sberbank data centres this month.
They contradict the Russian Defense Ministry's own reports that it began striking Ukrainian data centres last month.
Putin played down drone attacks on oil refineries, including a fire at Rosneft's Ryazan refinery on Thursday: 'Nothing particularly significant, but nevertheless they persist'.
He admitted Russian security services failed to anticipate attacks on commercial logistics hubs such as Wildberries and Ozon.
Earlier story: our 15 Oct 2026 edition (item 4) carried a Reuters report that Ukrainian drones hit Sberbank's Balakovo data centre after three attacks in the past week on Yandex data centres.
quote_evidence: President Vladimir Putin warned Thursday that Russia is actively retaliating in response to recent Ukrainian attacks on its data centers, while simultaneously brushing off recent drone attacks on oil refineries.

His first public comments acknowledging drone attacks targeting Yandex and Sberbank data centers this month contradict the Russian Defense Ministry’s own reports that it began striking Ukrainian data centers last month.
“They hit here and there. Nothing particularly significant, but nevertheless they persist,” the Russian leader said of the refinery attacks.
why_it_matters_hint: The Russian president has publicly confirmed that data centres are now targets in the war, in contrast to his own ministry's account.
notes: Follow-up of the 15 Oct 2026 edition's Sberbank data centre story. The article gives no damage figures. The Moscow Times says it is designated 'undesirable' in Russia.
